subject: pharmacology
title: Leprosy Pharmacology: Dapsone, Clofazimine, Rifampicin, MDT, Lepra Reactions and Thalidomide

steps.tx: **Dapsone**, a sulfone blocking folate synthesis exactly as sulfonamides do, was leprosy's first effective monotherapy and now serves inside multidrug therapy (MDT) and dermatology's neutrophilic dermatosis niches. Its signature toxicities are haematological: dose related haemolysis (dangerous and occasionally fatal in G6PD deficiency, screening argued by population), methaemoglobinaemia, and the dapsone hypersensitivity (sulfone) syndrome of fever, rash, hepatitis and lymphadenopathy at four to six weeks that demands immediate cessation.
steps.say: Dapsone is leprosy's sulfone elder: haemolysis in G6PD, sulfone syndrome at six weeks, stop on the rash.

left.title: Dapsone territory
points: Pneumocystis alternative in sulfa allergy history

steps.tx: **Dapsone**, a sulfone, blocks folate synthesis in the same manner as sulfonamides. It was the first effective drug used alone for leprosy and now belongs inside multidrug therapy and in some neutrophilic skin diseases. Dose related haemolysis is the signature blood toxicity and can be fatal when G6PD is deficient, which is why population screening is debated. Methaemoglobinaemia also occurs. The hypersensitivity, or sulfone, syndrome of fever, rash, hepatitis, and lymphadenopathy arrives at four to six weeks and demands that the drug stop immediately.
steps.say: Dapsone blocks folate synthesis like a sulfonamide and remains inside leprosy multidrug therapy. Haemolysis rises with dose and can be fatal if G6PD is deficient, and methaemoglobin can form as well. Fever, rash, hepatitis, and enlarged nodes at four to six weeks are sulfone syndrome, and the drug is stopped at once.

vis.alt: A red cell pathway shows dapsone blocking folate synthesis and haemolysis in G6PD deficiency.
vis.caption: Dapsone interrupts folate production in the organism while a G6PD deficient erythrocyte breaks down under oxidant stress. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Clofazimine**, a riminophenazine dye concentrating in macrophages and fat, kills Mycobacterium leprae slowly while its anti inflammatory action suppresses erythema nodosum leprosum, earning double duty in MDT and reactions. It stains skin red brown to near black (months to fade, darkest in lesions), discolours secretions, crystallises in gut with enteropathy at high doses, and prolongs QT inside resistant tuberculosis regimens where it moonlights. Patients warned about pigmentation complete therapy; patients surprised by it default.
steps.say: Clofazimine dyes the patient to cure them; warn about the colour or lose the adherence.

left.title: Clofazimine actions
points: Anti inflammatory in type 2 lepra reactions

right.title: Clofazimine burdens
points: Red brown skin pigmentation, slow to fade
Dry ichthyotic skin and eye discoloration
Gastrointestinal crystal enteropathy at high dose

steps.tx: **Rifampicin** in leprosy is prescribed by the month, not the day: a single supervised 600 mg monthly dose inside MDT exploits its bactericidal peak (killing 99.9 percent of viable bacilli per dose) while monthly spacing contains its enzyme induction and cost. Daily rifampicin has no place here, and its interactions still apply to the monthly pulse. The contrast with tuberculosis daily rifampicin is a favourite prescribing examination hinge.
steps.say: Leprosy rifampicin is monthly and supervised; tuberculosis rifampicin is daily. Do not cross the calendars.

nodes.label: Packs counted at each monthly collection

steps.tx: **Multidrug therapy** divides leprosy by bacterial load: paucibacillary (PB, up to five lesions, rifampicin monthly plus dapsone daily for six months) and multibacillary (MB, rifampicin plus clofazimine monthly supervised with clofazimine and dapsone daily for twelve months), free in WHO blister packs globally. Uniform MDT (all patients twelve months) is trialled in some programmes; classification by lesion count and slit skin smear where available assigns the pack.
steps.say: Count lesions, choose the pack: six months paucibacillary, twelve multibacillary, free everywhere.

left.title: Paucibacillary MDT
points: Single lesion: ROM single dose historically (below)

right.title: Multibacillary MDT
points: More than five lesions or smear positive

steps.tx: The **ROM regimen** (single dose rifampicin, ofloxacin and minocycline) treated single lesion paucibacillary leprosy in one supervised encounter, an adherence masterpiece whose niche narrowed as classification and uniform MDT evolved; ofloxacin and **minocycline** remain the alternative MDT components for rifampicin resistance, intolerance or contraindication, alongside clarithromycin in specialist constructions. Their existence matters when reactions or toxicity remove first line pieces mid course.
steps.say: ROM cured a single lesion in one visit; ofloxacin and minocycline are the spare parts shelf.

left.title: ROM concept
points: Superseded in many programmes by standard MDT

right.title: Alternative components
points: Ofloxacin daily in rifampicin sparing regimens

steps.tx: **Lepra reaction** type 1 (reversal reaction) is upgrading cell mediated immunity inflaming lesions and nerves, threatening function in days, treated by continuing MDT and adding prednisolone tapered over months with nerve function charted serially; steroids started late save less nerve, which makes reaction recognition a neurological emergency wearing dermatological clothes. Analgesia, splinting and physiotherapy ride with the steroid prescription.
steps.say: Type 1 reactions eat nerves quietly; prednisolone early and nerve charts monthly are the rescue.

nodes.label: Lesions inflame, nerves tender and weakening
Prednisolone started and tapered over months
Nerve function charted serially for recovery

steps.tx: A type 1 **lepra reaction**, the reversal reaction, is upgrading cell mediated immunity that inflames lesions and nerves and can cost nerve function within days. Multidrug therapy is continued. Prednisolone is added and tapered over months, and nerve function is charted serially, because steroids that start late save less nerve. Swollen lesions with a tender thickened nerve are therefore a neurological emergency wearing a skin disease's appearance. Analgesia, splinting, and physiotherapy accompany the steroid rather than waiting until the course ends.
steps.say: Type 1 reversal reactions inflame leprosy lesions and nerves as immunity improves, and function can be lost within days. Multidrug treatment continues and prednisolone is tapered across months. Nerve charts are repeated because a late start saves less function. Splints and physiotherapy go with the steroid.

vis.alt: Inflamed skin lesions and a thickened nerve are shown beside a tapering course of prednisolone.
vis.caption: A reversal reaction reddens and swells existing leprosy lesions and thickens a peripheral nerve while steroid dose steps downward over months. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Erythema nodosum leprosum** (ENL, type 2 reaction) is immune complex vasculitis in lepromatous disease: crops of tender nodules, fever, neuritis, iritis, orchitis and glomerulonephritis in waves for years. Mild disease takes NSAIDs; severe disease takes high dose prednisolone, clofazimine's anti inflammatory high dose, and **thalidomide**, the most effective agent, fenced by its teratogenic history behind absolute pregnancy prohibition and controlled distribution. ENL, not bacillary load, is where leprosy blinds and cripples treated patients.
steps.say: ENL is vasculitis in waves; thalidomide masters it behind the strictest pregnancy fence in pharmacology.

left.title: ENL management ladder
points: Mild: NSAIDs and reassurance, MDT continues
Moderate to severe: prednisolone high dose taper
Clofazimine escalated for anti inflammatory effect
Thalidomide for severe or steroid dependent disease

steps.tx: **Haemolysis in G6PD deficiency** and the **sulfone syndrome** close dapsone's safety liturgy with management: baseline G6PD testing where prevalence argues, haemoglobin and reticulocytes after starting, methaemoglobinaemia treated by cessation and methylene blue where symptomatic (itself G6PD fenced, from the anaesthetic lessons), and sulfone syndrome treated by immediate withdrawal and corticosteroids with weeks of vigilance. Alternative regimens without dapsone are built with ofloxacin and minocycline from the spare shelf above.
steps.say: Test, count, stop on the syndrome, and build the dapsone free regimen from ofloxacin and minocycline.

nodes.label: Fever, rash and hepatitis at weeks 4 to 6: stop dapsone
Steroids for syndrome, regimen rebuilt without dapsone
